issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry removes every LoggingHandler from the root logger as a global side effect
issues.detail: The shutdown path strips all OTLP LoggingHandler instances from the root logger to break a deadlock. This silently rips out handlers installed by user code, other subsystems, or multi-job hosts. Scope removal to the specific handler this module installed by holding an explicit reference, rather than mutating global logging state to fix a local problem.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer locates the OTLP handler by isinstance scan instead of holding a reference
issues.detail: Replay walks logging.getLogger().handlers and picks the first LoggingHandler found. If another OTLP handler exists, the replay targets the wrong sink; if none is found, the upload path silently no-ops, recreating the very failure mode this PR claims to fix. Store the handler created in _setup_cloud_tracer and replay into it directly.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler.buffer is an unbounded list of LogRecords
issues.detail: If a job hangs or crashes slowly before init_recording or _on_cleanup runs, the buffer grows without limit and can OOM the worker. Use a bounded structure (deque with maxlen, or byte cap) and drop oldest with a one-line warning on flush. A crash-log feature that exhausts memory is worse than the bug it fixes.

issues.description: Unrelated changes bundled: makefile -n auto removal, test_plugin_google_stt exclusion, worker.py race fix
issues.detail: The diff mixes the crash-log feature with a worker.py pending-assignment race fix and a makefile change dropping pytest-xdist plus a test file. None are mentioned in the PR description. Split into separate commits so bisect, revert, and review work, or at minimum document each with a one-line rationale.

issues.description: _on_cleanup catches bare Exception around init_recording, leaving partial telemetry state on failure
issues.detail: The except Exception clause logs and only stops buffering on the failure branch. If init_recording raises after partially wiring the OTLP pipeline, half-initialized state leaks into shutdown. Narrow the catch, and ensure _stop_log_buffering runs unconditionally so the handler frame is well-defined regardless of which step failed.

issues.description: Forcing _shutdown_fut to resolve on crash overloads its postcondition with crash signaling
issues.detail: _on_entry_done now sets _shutdown_fut with reason='job crashed' to unblock cleanup. Downstream consumers previously could assume orderly shutdown semantics; the same channel now carries crash signals. Either redefine the future's contract to include crash, or use a separate signal so control flow remains reasonable.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes a real bug — crash logs lost when sessions fail to start — and the overall shape (buffer early, replay through OTLP, force shutdown on crash) is correct. Two P0 defects undermine the fix: shutdown mutates the root logger globally by removing all OTLP LoggingHandlers, and replay locates its sink by isinstance scan rather than holding the handler reference it created. P1 concerns include an unbounded buffer, three unrelated changes smuggled into the diff (worker.py race fix, makefile parallelism removal, test exclusion), and a bare except that leaks half-initialized telemetry state. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — scope handler ownership, cap the buffer, split the patch.
